glossary.definition: Generative AI is the umbrella term for any AI that creates new content, text, images, audio, video, or code, rather than just sorting or analyzing things that already exist. A spam filter that sorts email into "junk" or "not junk" is not generative; a tool that writes you a brand new email from scratch is. It's called "generative" because it generates something that didn't exist a moment ago, the way a chef generates a new dish from raw ingredients rather than just plating a dish someone else already cooked.

items.title: Apple CEO says the company doesn’t ‘want to ship AI for AI’s sake’
items.summary: Apple's new CEO defended the company's current position in the AI landscape. During a recent interview with Wired’s Steven Levy , Apple CEO John Ternus defended the company’s current position in the AI landscape. Over the past couple years, Apple has often been described as behind on AI, especially as it delayed the release of a more powerful version of Siri, which finally launched this summer . ” Ternus added that Apple is “absolutely going to leverage AI” in its new products, but he said, “We don’t want to ship AI for AI’s sake.

items.title: Anthropic's watermark rollout leaves a loophole on two older Claude models
items.summary: Anthropic is expanding its text watermark to four more Claude models to meet the EU AI Act's December deadline. On the older models Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, developers can bypass the watermark by tweaking a single sampling parameter. Anthropic addresses the loophole with just a compliance warning. In an email to API customers, Anthropic said it will watermark Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, and Claude Sonnet 4.6.

items.title: Can enterprise AI pay for the boom?
items.summary: The artificial intelligence buildout is making an enormous bet on what businesses will eventually be willing to pay for intelligence. In our research this summer on forecasting the AI bubble, we argued that a key indicator to watch is productive utilization by enterprise customers. Specifically, we said at the time, if infrastructure supply catches up before productive monetization materializes, the risk of a bubble popping increases to what we felt were dangerous levels. We forecast that the supply constraints and healthy capital funding appetites at that time could provide conditions for a soft landing.

items.title: I built an AI Tamagotchi before Meta could
items.summary: Mark Zuckerberg's Meta made AI look so stinking cute by giving it a squishy little face - and this holiday season, he wants to sell you a Muse Charm so you can carry your jolly AI helper around like a Tamagotchi. But I won't be buying one, because we have Muse Charm at home . It cost just $50, and I've decided the learning experience was worth it. My version doesn't sport cameras or a 5G cellular radio , but it really talks to Muse and has cute avatars, too!

items.title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims
items.summary: Named “Volta-Autodoxer,” the recently uncovered malware uses AI tools to collect troves of data about victims, from login credentials and credit card numbers to Discord sessions and UberEats receipts. New research shared exclusively with Kernel Panic shows that hackers have started adding AI functionality into a new strain of infostealer malware , making it possible for the system to automatically profile victims and quickly surface the highest value targets and their information. Dubbed “Volta-Autodoxer” because of how the malware refers to itself internally, the finding by Cisco Talos researchers sheds light on the ways that commercial LLMs are being used to augment and enhance the capabilities of established types of malware. Often hidden in counterfeit software, infostealers are designed to live up to their name, grabbing usernames, passwords, authentication tokens, cookies, credit card data, and more from infected machines.

items.title: Are Boutique AI Firms India’s Next Big Thing?
items.summary: After a decade building and scaling product-led startups across fintech and insurance, Prateek Jogani set out in 2025 to find his next problem to solve. AI was the unavoidable frontier, and a closer look at the ecosystem revealed a disconnect between industry hype and on-the-ground reality. Speaking to leadership teams across mid-cap, growth-stage, and pre-IPO enterprises, Jogani noticed a recurring pattern in discussions. Almost nobody had AI doing meaningful work inside the business.

items.title: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China with iOS 27.3
items.summary: Apple will launch Apple Intelligence in China with iOS 27.3, the company announced on its Chinese newsroom website , as reported by MacRumors . The Apple Intelligence features will be available first in an iOS 27.3 beta that's set to launch on November 4th, with a full iOS 27.3 release scheduled for December. This launch doesn't bring the new Siri AI to China. Instead, Apple is launching several of its earlier Apple Intelligence features like notification summaries, real-time translation, rewriting and proofreading tools, visual intelligence, and removing objects from photos.

items.title: Dartmouth's provost warned us about AI cheating—but his own AI use cost him his job
items.summary: On August 9, 2026, Dartmouth College provost Santiago Schnell wrote a Washington Post op-ed called "Universities are fighting AI cheating. " This week, Schnell discovered the depths of the problem himself as he resigned from the university after an advisory committee found that he failed to disclose significant AI use in an academic paper and in the Washington Post op-ed, even though publishers required such disclosure. " He did turn over his Dartmouth laptop, but he did not turn over logs from his personal LLM accounts related to the writings in question. Nor did he agree to meet with the committee.

items.title: Smplify wants a human checkpoint between AI agents and your device fleet
items.summary: One of the great things about  Apple device management  solutions is that  the market for them is growing . Another is that because no two enterprises are alike, there is scope to bring different offerings to the market. I spoke with Ben Greiner, co-founder and COO of  Smplify , a new-to-market device management vendor, to find out what his company provides to IT. Smplify, which  just announced $1m in pre-seed funding , offers what could be described as a headless management tool: everything it does is available through the API and CLI.

items.title: Gemini Carbon aims to boost AI cyber defense, but is limited to a few
items.summary: The model addresses security concerns. Yet its exclusive release means most enterprises won’t be able to test it.

items.title: GitHub bets on multi-agent software development with Copilot overhaul
items.summary: GitHub is expanding Copilot beyond code generation and developer assistance, launching a redesigned Copilot app and a new Projects capability that enables teams to coordinate multiple AI agents, share context from tools and repositories, and manage software development workflows from a single platform. The updates to GitHub Copilot , announced at the company’s annual GitHub Universe conference, come at a time when enterprises are increasingly looking to deploy AI agents across software development workflows to accelerate coding, testing, and application maintenance. While the earlier version of the app focused primarily on helping developers run agent sessions, work on code changes, review diffs, and create pull requests, the updated app extends that experience beyond coding by serving as a central workspace for managing AI-driven software development and connecting agents with development tools and project context, the company wrote in a blog post . Developers will also be able to use the app to work on specifications, participate in design discussions, and analyze application telemetry alongside coding tasks, it added.
